check.title: Then it checks the work

findings.text: The rose gold and blush wash isn't Sephora's black and white.
findings.recommendation: Use black and white for layout, and let product color carry the image.

findings.text: "Glow Up Your Beauty Routine" is a generic line with no expert voice, and it doesn't mention Sephora Accelerate.
findings.recommendation: Write like a beauty advisor: specific, inclusive, and helpful.

findings.text: A posed group smiling at the camera doesn't match the photography style.
findings.recommendation: Use a candid photo of a real team at work from the photo library.

everyday.eyebrow: Use case 4 · Everyday guidelines, inside your office applications
everyday.title: The right tone in every email and deck
everyday.sub: Most of {name} will never open a brand portal. With Frontify connected, your AI assistant inside your email and presentation apps reads the Everyday guidelines and checks the work before it goes out.
everyday.note: Your agent embedded in your enterprise apps, usually ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot, or Gemini, can read Frontify guidelines and use them as a reference and rule set for any suggested changes. Sample email, presentation, and guidelines.

tabs.label: Email
tabs.ask: Check this email against our email tone of voice before I send it.
tabs.intro: Three fixes based on **Everyday › Email tone of voice**:

before.subject: Following up
body: Hi team, just circling back on the below!!
We've been heads-down on Sephora Accelerate and there's a lot going on, so I wanted to share where things stand.
Can you review the launch plan by Thursday?

after.subject: Review the Accelerate plan by Thursday
body: Hi team, can you review the Accelerate plan by Thursday?
It covers the messaging, launch assets, and timeline. Comments in the doc are perfect.

fixes.label: Subject:
fixes.note: say what you need. "Following up" doesn't.

fixes.label: Opening:
fixes.note: lead with the ask. It's in the last line right now.

fixes.label: Sign-off:
fixes.note: use the standard signature, with no quotes.

tabs.done: Updated. The draft matches the email tone of voice and is ready to send.

placements.label: Window
placements.where: Both windows, centered at eye level.
placements.content: Campaign art and the headline. No prices in the window.
placements.ask: Where do the holiday price cards go?
placements.answer: Inside the store, never in the window. **Windows carry the campaign art and headline only.** The price cards from the mailer go on the gifting table and the end caps.

placements.label: Gifting table
placements.where: Front edge of the gifting table, facing the entrance.
placements.content: Headline and one line of copy. Gift sets only on the table, refreshed every Monday.
placements.ask: What goes on the gifting table this week?
placements.answer: **Holiday gifting** sets, with the **header facing the entrance**. Refresh the table every Monday.

placements.label: Shelf
placements.where: Top of each end cap, at eye level.
placements.content: One product story per card, never two.
placements.ask: Can one end cap card cover two brands?
placements.answer: **No. One product story per card.** Give the second brand its own end cap.

placements.label: Register
placements.where: Left of the register, angled toward the guest.
placements.content: One add-on offer. The queue fixtures get price strips only, no posters.
placements.ask: What sign goes at the register this month?
placements.answer: One **counter card, left of the register**, angled toward the guest. For Holiday gifting it is Add a gift card. Queue fixtures get **price strips only**.
